chunks: From him (Al-Hilli) from Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Hanan ibn Sadir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked, and I was present,

About a lamb that nursed from a pig until it grew up and its bones became strong, then a man bred it with his sheep, and offspring were produced for him. What do you say about its offspring? He said, 'As for what you recognize of its offspring by its own eye (distinctive features), do not approach it; and as for what you do not recognize, it is like cheese, so eat it and do not ask about it.'

key_terms.اِسْتَفْحَلَهُ: He bred it / He mated it
key_terms.بِعَيْنِهِ: By its own eye / Distinctive features

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the offspring of an animal that nursed from a pig?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) applied to animal lineage, distinguishing between visible morphological traits and inherent purity. Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while offspring inheriting distinct 'pig' characteristics remain impure, those without such visible markers are treated as permissible (*halal*), akin to cheese, reflecting a pragmatic approach to dietary laws. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on observable evidence (*'ayn*) in determining the status of mixed-species offspring.
